question: At K=4 and high total horizon T, does sequential recentering outperform a fixed pi_1 reference on matched first-actor/critic trajectories?

branches.recenter: pi_2 <- pi_1, pi_3 <- pi_2, pi_4 <- pi_3 (each freshly updated in the same scheduled actor step)
branches.fixed_ref: pi_2, pi_3, pi_4 each reference the freshly updated pi_1; every actor still receives one update

host_assignment: For zero-based environment index i and seed s, assign (i+s)%2==0 to svcho and the other pairs to choi; keep recenter and fixed_ref of a pair on the same host. Both hosts run every T in each stage.
primary_outcome: Paired d4rl_pi4(recenter)-d4rl_pi4(fixed_ref) at T=4,7 by environment and seed. Display all nine task effects and overall equal-task effect for each T; do not select favorable tasks/seeds.
boundary_outcome: Same signed contrast at T=10, reported separately as a boundary test.
identity_gate: First two actors and optimizer states, critic and optimizer state, targets, RNG and normalization match exactly between arms in every paired checkpoint; all four actors have equal update counts.

pilot.purpose: Check host wiring and pair checkpoint invariants separately on each host. Not a performance test.

missing_or_failed_runs: Retain missing/incomplete pairs in summaries, never substitute earlier K4 scores or transfer checkpoints from another host.
interpretation: A consistent signed effect at T=4,7 tests whether recentering broadens the high-T plateau at K=4 under this shared-driver protocol. T=10 measures where benefit persists or fails; no null result proves equivalence.
